title: Man shot after North York killing: [Toronto Edition]
article: Residents of a North York townhouse complex are trying to come to grips with the horrific violence that left a woman dead and her daughter in a hospital clinging to life.
Neighbours are organizing a community barbecue to raise spirits and money for the family of the dead woman they knew as "Nana."
The woman, health-care professional Pandora Whyte, 62, and her daughter Marcia Allyne, 37, were attacked with a knife by Ucal Lauzon shortly before 11 p.m. on Friday, according to media reports.
Minutes later, Toronto police shot and killed Mr. Lauzon, the dead woman's 34-year-old adopted brother, after a confrontation.
Neighbours say they heard police order him to drop his weapon before they fired.
The Special Investigations Unit has taken over the case.
Ms. Whyte's grandson paced the parking lot yesterday behind his grandmother's Sheppard Avenue West townhouse, still surrounded by police tape.
The distraught young man who did not give his name said: "I want \[Lauzon\] to be alive ... This guy got off too easy."
A neighbour who identified himself as Kevin said Mr. Lauzon seemed like a "good guy."
Mr. Lauzon worked in a cookie factory and made t-shirts for his own clothing design, said Kevin, a friend of one of Ms. Whyte's grandsons.

Kevin said he and another neighbour saw Ms. Whyte slumped over on her couch covered in blood through her glass patio door; he said he then saw Mr. Lauzon attacking Ms. Allyne. He did not see a knife but said Ms. Allyne fought back -- kicking and scratching.
He said he tried to grab Mr. Lauzon from outside, yelling, "Come on!"
"He was calm. He looked at us and just closed the door."
Kevin and his neighbour shattered one glass door in an effort to get at him.

A Special Investigations Unit press release said police found Ms. Allyne outside the home suffering from severe stab wounds. She is in critical condition at Sunnybrook and Women's College Health Sciences Centre.
Ms. Whyte's 16-year-old adopted daughter, Rochelle, was in the home when the violence began, neighbours say.
She ran to Amira Wardak, who lives a few doors down -- her clothing soaked in her adopted mother's blood -- and told her, "My uncle hit my mom," Ms. Wardak said.
She said Rochelle was able to escape after several neighbours stood in between her and Mr. Lauzon, who tried to drag her back inside.
Neighbours say Ms. Whyte was a long-time resident. They will hold a barbecue in the parking lot behind the complex next Saturday to collect money to help with funeral arrangements.
"The whole community feels like we lost a part of our family," Ms. Wardak said.
